subproblem.title: Pairwise disjoint open neighbourhoods of the open unit faces (step 1)
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ. For an index pair p = (ι, b) with ι : Fin k → Fin P and b : Fin P → ℤ, let Φ_p : Euclid k → Euclid P be Φ_p(y) := b + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} (Lean: WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)), where e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1. Let Q₁ := {y ∈ Euclid k : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i} and Cᵏ := {y ∈ Euclid k : 0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1 for all i}. Assume the separation property (S): for all index pairs p ≠ q whose first components are strictly increasing, all y ∈ Q₁ and all y' ∈ Cᵏ, either 1 ≤ dist(Φ_p y, Φ_q y') or min(y_j, 1 − y_j) ≤ dist(Φ_p y, Φ_q y') for some j ∈ Fin k. Then there is a family (N_p) of subsets of Euclid P, indexed by all index pairs, such that for every index pair p with strictly increasing first component: N_p is open; Φ_p(y) ∈ N_p for every y ∈ Q₁; and for every index pair q ≠ p with strictly increasing first component, Φ_q(y) ∉ N_p for every y ∈ Cᵏ, and N_p ∩ N_q = ∅.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ), (∀ p q : (Fin k → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ), StrictMono p.1 → StrictMono q.1 → p ≠ q → ∀ y y' : Euclid k, (∀ j, 0 < y j ∧ y j < 1) → (∀ i, 0 ≤ y' i ∧ y' i ≤ 1) → 1 ≤ dist (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (q.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y' j • EuclideanSpace.single (q.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) ∨ ∃ j, min (y j) (1 - y j) ≤ dist (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (q.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y' j • EuclideanSpace.single (q.1 j) (1 : ℝ))) → ∃ N : (Fin k → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ) → Set (Euclid P), ∀ p : (Fin k → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ), StrictMono p.1 → IsOpen (N p) ∧ (∀ y : Euclid k, (∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1) → (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) ∈ N p) ∧ ∀ q : (Fin k → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ), StrictMono q.1 → q ≠ p → (∀ y : Euclid k, (∀ i, 0 ≤ y i ∧ y i ≤ 1) → (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (q.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (q.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) ∉ N p) ∧ Disjoint (N p) (N q)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the supplied proof of the selected theorem dimred_mbl_dtfr_boundary_variation (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1, chapter-06.txt lines 1840–1857, where Q is analysed near the interior F̆ of each face; the parent makes the neighbourhoods explicit and pairwise disjoint), for an arbitrary dimension k. In the selected theorem, (S) is clause (c) of the sibling face_geometry; here it is a hypothesis. The parent's N_p is the set of x with t := p̃_p(x) ∈ Q₁ and dist(x, Φ_p t) < δ(t)/2, where δ(t) = min(1, min_j min(t_j, 1 − t_j)). Its arguments (i) and (ii) only use that some t ∈ Q₁ satisfies dist(x, Φ_p t) < δ(t)/2. So we take N_p to be the union, over all t ∈ Q₁, of these balls (dropping the projection condition t = p̃_p(x)), and we write the radius δ(t)/2 as finitely many strict inequalities. This needs no projection, no finite minimum and no continuity argument.

Notation. Φ_p, Q₁, Cᵏ are as in the statement. An index pair is admissible if its first component is strictly increasing.

1. Definition. For an index pair p and t ∈ Q₁ let
 B_p(t) := {x ∈ Euclid P : 2·dist(x, Φ_p t) < 1} ∩ ⋂_{j ∈ Fin k} {x : 2·dist(x, Φ_p t) < min(t_j, 1 − t_j)},
 and let N_p := ⋃_{t ∈ Q₁} B_p(t). In Lean: N := fun p => ⋃ t ∈ {t : Euclid k | ∀ j, 0 < t j ∧ t j < 1}, {x | 2 * dist x (Φ p t) < 1} ∩ ⋂ j, {x | 2 * dist x (Φ p t) < min (t j) (1 - t j)}. Thus x ∈ N_p iff some t ∈ Q₁ has 2·dist(x, Φ_p t) < 1 and 2·dist(x, Φ_p t) < min(t_j, 1 − t_j) for every j.
2. N_p is open. For fixed p and t, the map x ↦ 2·dist(x, Φ_p t) is continuous (continuous_const.mul (continuous_id.dist continuous_const)). So each set {x : 2·dist(x, Φ_p t) < c} with c constant is open (isOpen_lt). B_p(t) is one such set intersected with a finite intersection of such sets over the finite type Fin k (isOpen_iInter_of_finite, IsOpen.inter), so it is open. N_p is a union of open sets (isOpen_biUnion), so it is open.
3. The open face lies in N_p. Let y ∈ Q₁ and take t := y. Then dist(Φ_p y, Φ_p t) = 0, and 2·0 = 0 < 1. Also 0 < min(y_j, 1 − y_j) for every j, because 0 < y_j < 1 (lt_min_iff, sub_pos). Hence Φ_p(y) ∈ B_p(y) ⊆ N_p.
4. Key inequality. Let p, q be admissible with q ≠ p, let t ∈ Q₁, y' ∈ Cᵏ and x ∈ B_p(t), and put D := dist(Φ_p t, Φ_q y'). Then 2·dist(x, Φ_p t) < D. Indeed, (S) applies to (p, q, t, y'), since p ≠ q by symmetry of ≠.
 - If 1 ≤ D, use 2·dist(x, Φ_p t) < 1.
 - If min(t_j, 1 − t_j) ≤ D for some j, use 2·dist(x, Φ_p t) < min(t_j, 1 − t_j).
5. Other closed faces avoid N_p. Let p, q be admissible with q ≠ p and let y ∈ Cᵏ. Suppose x := Φ_q(y) ∈ N_p, say x ∈ B_p(t) with t ∈ Q₁. Step 4 with y' := y gives 2·dist(x, Φ_p t) < dist(Φ_p t, Φ_q y) = dist(x, Φ_p t) (dist_comm). This is impossible, since dist(x, Φ_p t) ≥ 0. Hence Φ_q(y) ∉ N_p.
6. Disjointness. Let p, q be admissible with q ≠ p. Suppose x ∈ N_p ∩ N_q, say x ∈ B_p(t) and x ∈ B_q(t') with t, t' ∈ Q₁, and put D := dist(Φ_p t, Φ_q t').
 - Since t' ∈ Q₁ ⊆ Cᵏ (the strict inequalities imply the weak ones), step 4 for (p, q, t, t') gives 2·dist(x, Φ_p t) < D.
 - Since t ∈ Q₁ ⊆ Cᵏ, step 4 with p and q exchanged gives 2·dist(x, Φ_q t') < dist(Φ_q t', Φ_p t) = D. Here q is admissible, p ≠ q, x ∈ B_q(t') and y' := t.
 - By the triangle inequality (dist_triangle, dist_comm), D ≤ dist(Φ_p t, x) + dist(x, Φ_q t') < D/2 + D/2 = D, a contradiction.
 Hence N_p ∩ N_q = ∅, i.e. Disjoint (N p) (N q) (Set.disjoint_left).
7. Conclusion. Steps 2, 3, 5 and 6 give the four required properties, for every admissible p and every admissible q ≠ p. For k = 0 nothing changes: the intersections over j are all of Euclid P, Q₁ = Cᵏ is the one-point space, and only the alternative 1 ≤ D of (S) can occur. ∎
proof_key_steps: N_p := ⋃_{t∈Q₁} {x : 2·dist(x, Φ_p t) < 1 and 2·dist(x, Φ_p t) < min(t_j, 1 − t_j) for all j}. It is a union of finite intersections of open sets, hence open, and it contains Φ_p(Q₁) (take t = y).
(S) gives 2·dist(x, Φ_p t) < dist(Φ_p t, Φ_q y') whenever x lies in the t-piece of N_p, q ≠ p is admissible and y' ∈ [0,1]^k.
Taking x = Φ_q y' gives a contradiction, so Φ_q([0,1]^k) ∩ N_p = ∅.
Applying the inequality for (p, q) and for (q, p), together with the triangle inequality, gives N_p ∩ N_q = ∅.

audit.reason: The prose and exact type match. The explicit open-ball union contains each open face. Separation excludes other closed faces; applying separation in both directions and the triangle inequality proves disjointness. The proof includes k = 0 and uses only its stated separation hypothesis.

subproblem.title: Superadditivity of local mass over a finite pairwise disjoint family (step 9)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ Euclid P be any set, and let S be an n-current in U (GeometricCurrentOn U n). Let ι be a type, s a finite subset of ι, and N : ι → Set (Euclid P) with N_i ∩ N_j = ∅ for all distinct i, j ∈ s. Then Σ_{i∈s} M_{N_i}(S) ≤ M_{⋃_{i∈s} N_i}(S) in [0, ∞]. Here M_W(S) = S.massOn W is the supremum of ofReal(S ω) over the test n-forms ω in U (TestFormOn U n) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x (Simon 6.2.5).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ι : Type) (s : Finset ι) (N : ι → Set (Euclid P)), (↑s : Set ι).PairwiseDisjoint N → ∑ i ∈ s, S.massOn (N i) ≤ S.massOn (⋃ i ∈ s, N i)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 9 of the supplied proof of the selected theorem, where Σ_p V_p ≤ M(∂Q₀) is obtained by gluing near-optimal forms on the pairwise disjoint N_p. This is the summation over faces in Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1, after (32) (chapter-06.txt lines 1888–1899). Here the argument is stated for an arbitrary current and an arbitrary finite pairwise disjoint family, with the union W in place of ℝ^P.

Notation. W := ⋃_{i∈s} N_i. |·| := covectorEuclideanNorm. Adm(A) := massAdmissibleOn U n A = {ω ∈ TestFormOn U n : tsupport ω ⊆ A and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x}. M_A(S) := S.massOn A = sSup{ofReal(S ω) : ω ∈ Adm(A)}.

1. Gluing. Let ω_i ∈ Adm(N_i) for i ∈ s, and let ω := Σ_{i∈s} ω_i, a sum in the submodule TestFormOn U n. Its underlying form is Σ_{i∈s} ω_i (Submodule.coe_sum), so ω(x) = Σ_{i∈s} ω_i(x) (Finset.sum_apply). We claim ω ∈ Adm(W) and S(ω) = Σ_{i∈s} S(ω_i).
 (a) S is linear, so S(ω) = Σ_{i∈s} S(ω_i) (map_sum).
 (b) support ω ⊆ ⋃_{i∈s} support ω_i ⊆ ⋃_{i∈s} tsupport ω_i (Finset.sum_fn, Finset.support_sum, subset_tsupport). The last set is a finite union of closed sets, hence closed (isClosed_biUnion_finset). So tsupport ω = closure(support ω) ⊆ ⋃_{i∈s} tsupport ω_i ⊆ ⋃_{i∈s} N_i = W (closure_minimal).
 (c) Fix x. If ω_i(x) = 0 for every i ∈ s, then ω(x) = 0 and |ω(x)| = 0 ≤ 1 (covectorEuclideanNorm_zero). Otherwise pick i₀ ∈ s with ω_{i₀}(x) ≠ 0. Then x ∈ support ω_{i₀} ⊆ tsupport ω_{i₀} ⊆ N_{i₀}. For i ∈ s with i ≠ i₀, ω_i(x) ≠ 0 would give x ∈ N_i in the same way, contradicting N_i ∩ N_{i₀} = ∅. Hence ω(x) = ω_{i₀}(x) (Finset.sum_eq_single) and |ω(x)| ≤ 1.
2. Trivial case. If M_W(S) = ∞, the claim holds (le_top). Assume from now on that M_W(S) ≠ ∞. For i ∈ s we have N_i ⊆ W, so M_{N_i}(S) ≤ M_W(S) (massOn_mono) and M_{N_i}(S) ≠ ∞. Put V_i := M_{N_i}(S).toReal ≥ 0. Then ofReal(V_i) = M_{N_i}(S) (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal).
3. Near-optimal forms. Let η > 0 and i ∈ s. We find ω_i ∈ Adm(N_i) with V_i − η ≤ S(ω_i).
 - If V_i ≤ η, take ω_i := 0. It lies in Adm(N_i), since tsupport 0 = ∅ and |0| = 0 ≤ 1, and S(0) = 0 ≥ V_i − η.
 - If V_i > η, then 0 ≤ V_i − η < V_i = M_{N_i}(S).toReal, so ofReal(V_i − η) < M_{N_i}(S) (ENNReal.ofReal_lt_iff_lt_toReal). By lt_sSup_iff, some ω_i ∈ Adm(N_i) has ofReal(V_i − η) < ofReal(S ω_i). This forces V_i − η < S(ω_i) (ENNReal.ofReal_lt_ofReal_iff').
4. Glue. Choose such ω_i for every i ∈ s (choose). By step 1, ω := Σ_{i∈s} ω_i ∈ Adm(W). So ofReal(S ω) ≤ M_W(S) (le_massOn), and since M_W(S) ≠ ∞, S(ω) ≤ M_W(S).toReal (ENNReal.ofReal_le_iff_le_toReal). Hence
 Σ_{i∈s} V_i − |s|·η = Σ_{i∈s}(V_i − η) ≤ Σ_{i∈s} S(ω_i) = S(ω) ≤ M_W(S).toReal,
 using Finset.sum_le_sum, Finset.sum_sub_distrib, Finset.sum_const and nsmul_eq_mul. So Σ_{i∈s} V_i ≤ M_W(S).toReal + |s|·η.
5. Limit. Let ε > 0. If s = ∅, step 4 with η := 1 gives Σ_{i∈s} V_i ≤ M_W(S).toReal ≤ M_W(S).toReal + ε. Otherwise, step 4 with η := ε/|s| > 0 gives Σ_{i∈s} V_i ≤ M_W(S).toReal + ε. Hence Σ_{i∈s} V_i ≤ M_W(S).toReal (le_of_forall_pos_le_add).
6. Conclusion. Σ_{i∈s} M_{N_i}(S) = Σ_{i∈s} ofReal(V_i) = ofReal(Σ_{i∈s} V_i) ≤ ofReal(M_W(S).toReal) = M_W(S). The second equality uses ENNReal.ofReal_sum_of_nonneg and V_i ≥ 0; the inequality uses ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal and step 5; the last equality uses ENNReal.ofReal_toReal. ∎
proof_key_steps: Admissible forms ω_i for the pairwise disjoint N_i have at most one nonzero value at each point. So Σ ω_i is admissible for W = ⋃ N_i, and S(Σ ω_i) = Σ S(ω_i).
If M_W(S) = ∞ there is nothing to prove. Otherwise every M_{N_i}(S) is finite; put V_i := M_{N_i}(S).toReal.
Choose ω_i ∈ Adm(N_i) with S(ω_i) ≥ V_i − η (the zero form if V_i ≤ η, otherwise lt_sSup_iff) and glue them: Σ V_i − |s|η ≤ M_W(S).toReal.
Let η → 0 and convert back to [0, ∞] with ofReal.

subproblem.title: Admissible test form with prescribed values on a face (steps 5–6)
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1. Let p = (ι, b) be an index pair with ι : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing and b : Fin P → ℤ. Write e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1, Φ_p(y) := b + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} (Lean: WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)), and Q₁ := (0,1)ⁿ = {y ∈ Euclid n : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}. Let N ⊆ Euclid P be open with Φ_p(y) ∈ N for every y ∈ Q₁. Let g : Euclid n → Euclid n be C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞), smooth but not necessarily analytic), with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and ‖g(y)‖ ≤ 1 for all y (Euclidean norm of Euclid n). Then there is a test m-form γ on Euclid P (γ ∈ TestFormOn univ m) such that: tsupport γ ⊆ N; covectorEuclideanNorm(γ(x)) ≤ 1 for all x; and for every y ∈ Euclid n and every i ∈ Fin n, g(y)_i = (−1)^i · γ(Φ_p y)(fun l => e_{ι(i.succAbove l)}). In words, the i-th component of g(y) is (−1)^i times γ(Φ_p y) evaluated on (e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(m)}) with its i-th vector removed.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (p : (Fin (m + 1) → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ)) (N : Set (Euclid P)) (g : Euclid (m + 1) → Euclid (m + 1)), StrictMono p.1 → IsOpen N → (∀ y : Euclid (m + 1), (∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1) → (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) ∈ N) → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) g → HasCompactSupport g → tsupport g ⊆ {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} → (∀ y, ‖g y‖ ≤ 1) → ∃ γ : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, tsupport (γ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) ⊆ N ∧ (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((γ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) x) ≤ 1) ∧ ∀ (y : Euclid (m + 1)) (i : Fin (m + 1)), g y i = (-1 : ℝ) ^ (i : ℕ) * (γ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k => (p.2 k : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (fun l => EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 (Fin.succAbove i l)) (1 : ℝ))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 5 and 6 of the supplied proof of the selected theorem. Those steps build the cut-off χ around Kg = Φ_p(tsupport g) and the test form γ := χ·Σ_j g_j(p̃_p ·) ε_j, prove that γ is admissible, and compute its values on the face p, which feed face_divergence. These are the forms that realise the BV estimate of Simon Ch. 6, 2.35 and (28) (chapter-06.txt lines 606ff. and 1851–1857). Because χ = 1 on Kg, the field G(y) := χ(Φ_p y)·g(y) of parent step 6 equals g identically. So the face identity proved here is exactly the hypothesis of face_divergence with G := g. The ε_j come from the sibling face_covectors (Submission.cmcdtfrbv_face_covectors).

Notation. p = (ι, b), n := m + 1, e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1, Φ := Φ_p, Q₁ := (0,1)ⁿ, and |·| := covectorEuclideanNorm. Let π : Euclid P → Euclid n be π(x) := (x_{ι(j)} − b_{ι(j)})_j (Lean: WithLp.toLp 2 (fun j => x (ι j) - (b (ι j) : ℝ))). This is the parent's p̃_p. Throughout, C^∞ means ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞), the order of the hypothesis on g. In Lean write this order explicitly as (⊤ : ℕ∞); the scoped notation ∞ for it requires open scoped ContDiff.

1. The face map and its left inverse.
 - Φ is continuous: it is a constant plus a finite sum of the continuous maps y ↦ y_j • e_{ι(j)} (continuous_finsetSum, PiLp.continuous_apply).
 - π is C^∞. By contDiff_piLp it suffices that each coordinate x ↦ x_{ι(j)} − b_{ι(j)} is C^∞, and it is: a coordinate (contDiff_piLp_apply) minus a constant.
 - π(Φ(y)) = y for every y. The ι(j)-th coordinate of Φ(y) is b_{ι(j)} + Σ_{j'} y_{j'}·[ι(j) = ι(j')] = b_{ι(j)} + y_j, because ι is injective. (Lemmas: PiLp.add_apply, PiLp.toLp_apply, WithLp.ofLp_sum, Finset.sum_apply, PiLp.smul_apply, PiLp.single_apply, StrictMono.injective, Finset.sum_ite_eq.)
2. The compact set. K := Φ(tsupport g) is compact, as the continuous image of the compact set tsupport g (HasCompactSupport g). Also K ⊆ N, because tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and Φ(Q₁) ⊆ N.
3. The cut-off.
 - N is open and K is compact, so there is r > 0 with cthickening(r, K) ⊆ N (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open).
 - Apply exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff with order n := ⊤ : ℕ∞, i.e. C^∞, to the open set thickening(r, K) (isOpen_thickening) and the closed set K ⊆ thickening(r, K) (IsCompact.isClosed, self_subset_thickening). It gives a C^∞ map χ : Euclid P → ℝ with range in [0, 1], support χ = thickening(r, K), and χ(x) = 1 ⟺ x ∈ K.
 - tsupport χ = closure(thickening(r, K)) ⊆ cthickening(r, K) ⊆ N (closure_thickening_subset_cthickening).
 - χ has compact support: tsupport χ is closed and lies in the compact set cthickening(r, K) (IsCompact.cthickening, IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset).
 The parent used the radii r, 2r and 3r so that χ = 1 near K. Here χ = 1 on K suffices.
4. The covectors. Apply face_covectors to P, m and ι and choose ε : Fin n → Covector (Euclid P) m such that, for all c : Fin n → ℝ and i ∈ Fin n:
 (a) |Σ_j c_j ε_j| = √(Σ_j c_j²);
 (b) (Σ_{j'} c_{j'} ε_{j'})(fun l => e_{ι(i.succAbove l)}) = (−1)^i c_i.
5. The form. Define γ(x) := Σ_j (χ(x)·g(π x)_j) • ε_j (Lean: fun x => ∑ j, (χ x * g (π x) j) • ε j).
 - γ is C^∞. Each coefficient x ↦ χ(x)·g(π x)_j is the product (ContDiff.mul) of χ and the j-th coordinate (contDiff_piLp_apply) of g ∘ π (ContDiff.comp), so it is C^∞. Multiplying by the constant covector ε_j (ContDiff.smul_const) and taking the finite sum (ContDiff.sum) keep it C^∞.
 - support γ ⊆ support χ: if χ(x) = 0, every coefficient vanishes and γ(x) = 0. Hence γ has compact support (HasCompactSupport.mono), and tsupport γ ⊆ tsupport χ ⊆ N (closure_mono and step 3).
 - So γ is smooth with compact support and tsupport γ ⊆ univ. Together with these proofs it is an element of TestFormOn univ m whose underlying form is γ.
6. The norm bound. Fix x and put c_j := χ(x)·g(π x)_j. By (a), |γ(x)| = √(Σ_j c_j²). Now Σ_j c_j² = χ(x)²·Σ_j g(π x)_j² = χ(x)²·‖g(π x)‖² (EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq). Since 0 ≤ χ(x) ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ ‖g(π x)‖ ≤ 1, this is at most 1. Hence |γ(x)| ≤ 1 (Real.sqrt_le_one).
7. The face values. Fix y ∈ Euclid n and i ∈ Fin n. Apply (b) with c_j := χ(Φ y)·g(π(Φ y))_j, and use π(Φ y) = y (step 1):
 γ(Φ y)(fun l => e_{ι(i.succAbove l)}) = (−1)^i·χ(Φ y)·g(y)_i.
 Multiply by (−1)^i and use ((−1)^i)² = 1: (−1)^i·γ(Φ y)(fun l => e_{ι(i.succAbove l)}) = χ(Φ y)·g(y)_i.
 - If y ∈ tsupport g, then Φ y ∈ K, so χ(Φ y) = 1 and the right side is g(y)_i.
 - If y ∉ tsupport g, then g(y) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport), and both sides are 0.
 Hence g(y)_i = (−1)^i·γ(Φ y)(fun l => e_{ι(i.succAbove l)}) for all y and i.
8. By steps 5–7, γ ∈ TestFormOn univ m satisfies tsupport γ ⊆ N, |γ(x)| ≤ 1 for every x, and the face identity. No case split is needed for tsupport g = ∅ (then K = ∅ and χ = 0) or for m = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: π(x) := (x_{ι(j)} − b_{ι(j)})_j is C^∞ with π ∘ Φ_p = id, and K := Φ_p(tsupport g) is a compact subset of N.
Choose r > 0 with cthickening(r, K) ⊆ N. A C^∞ cut-off χ with values in [0,1], support χ = thickening(r, K) and χ = 1 exactly on K has compact tsupport contained in N.
γ(x) := Σ_j χ(x)·g(π x)_j·ε_j, with ε from face_covectors, is a test m-form with tsupport γ ⊆ N and |γ(x)| = |χ(x)|·‖g(π x)‖ ≤ 1.
By face_covectors (b) and χ = 1 on K, (−1)^i·γ(Φ_p y)(E_p ∘ succAbove i) = χ(Φ_p y)·g(y)_i = g(y)_i for all y and i.
